verdict.rationale: Browser Use publishes per-browser-hour pricing ($0.02/hour plus $5/GB residential proxy) and agent pricing as model cost +20% plus browser time, on pay-as-you-go credits. Its docs also set out concurrency tiers: 10 concurrent browsers free, 50 after a $100 top-up, and 250/500/1,000 at higher totals paid. missing for 10: documented API request-rate limits beyond concurrency, an explicit per-model price table for agent tasks, independent corroboration of the pricing and limits.

support.subject: As a developer, I can see transparent per-task or per-browser-hour pricing and documented rate/concurrency limits before committing

citations.quote: Browsers $0.02 / hour Cloud browsers, plus $5 / GB residential proxy.
Browser agents Model +20% Web agents, plus browser time and traffic.
Pay as you go. No subscription. Credits never expire.
new projects get 10 concurrent browsers at $0; a $100 one-time top-up (non-expiring credits, no subscription) unlocks 50 concurrent
